why: Every one of the 16 imported tables is inserted row-by-row with an individual `await ...insert(...)` inside a for loop instead of Drift's batch()/insertAll for same-shape bulk writes (lines 538-901). The whole thing is correctly wrapped in one _database.transaction() (DB-2 satisfied), but each row still pays its own round-trip; a family with several years of daily completions (thousands of completionEvents/learningLedger rows) multiplies import wall-clock time by roughly the row count instead of running as a handful of batched statements. Same dormant-code caveat as the delete-scoping finding in this file: no production caller exists yet, so this is a design defect ready to bite the first real user of a to-be-built restore feature, not an active incident.
recommendation: Replace each per-table loop with _database.batch((b) => b.insertAll(_database.<table>, rows)) inside the existing transaction.
acceptance_criteria: Import of a large fixture (1,000+ completionEvents) uses batch()/insertAll, verifiable by code review confirming no remaining bare `for` + `await ...insert(` loop in importData(), or by an insert-call-count assertion in a test.
